10
items.instruction: Source-backed adapted practice. Write a paragraph of about 150 words on "The Life of a Farmer".
answers: A farmer grows the food on which our everyday lives depend. In Bangladesh, farmers cultivate rice, vegetables, fruit and many other crops. Their work begins with preparing the soil and choosing suitable seeds. They must then water the fields, control pests responsibly and wait for the harvest. Rain, drought, floods and changes in market prices can make their income uncertain. Not all farmers own the land they cultivate, and some struggle to meet production costs. Better storage, fair access to markets, reliable advice and affordable finance can improve their position. Consumers can help by valuing agricultural work and reducing food waste. Farming also requires knowledge, planning and careful observation of nature. A farmer is therefore not merely a producer of crops but an important contributor to the nation's food security and economy. We should respect this work and support safer, more sustainable agriculture.

A flag represents all citizens, whatever their religion, occupation or background. We must handle it with care and follow the appropriate rules for its display. To me, respecting our national flag means trying to become a responsible and considerate citizen of Bangladesh.

Smoke from vehicles and factories can reduce air quality, while untreated waste can pollute rivers and canals. Plastic litter blocks drains and harms animals. These problems affect health, livelihoods and the natural systems on which people depend. Their causes are often connected with careless consumption, weak waste management and poor enforcement of reasonable standards. Individual action matters, but households cannot solve every problem alone. Authorities and businesses must provide effective waste collection, cleaner production and safe public transport. Students can reduce unnecessary plastic, separate waste where facilities exist and take part in supervised clean-up activities. We should also avoid burning rubbish and wasting water or electricity. Protecting the environment is not a task for one special day. It requires practical habits, reliable information and cooperation throughout the year so that everyone can live in healthier surroundings.

items.instruction: Source-backed adapted practice. Write a paragraph of about 150 words on "Preventing and Responding to Dengue".
answers: Dengue is a viral illness transmitted mainly through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. Preventing mosquito breeding is an important part of reducing its spread. We should empty or cover containers that collect water and help keep the surroundings free from discarded items that can hold rainwater. Suitable mosquito protection can reduce bites, including during daytime. A person with fever or other worrying symptoms should seek advice from a qualified health professional rather than rely on social-media remedies. Warning signs such as severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or bleeding require urgent medical attention. Medicines should be taken only with appropriate advice; some commonly used painkillers are unsuitable when dengue is suspected. Schools and local authorities can organise practical awareness activities and regular inspections of shared spaces. answers: The internet connects people with information and services across the world. Students can read books, attend lessons, communicate with teachers and explore subjects beyond their textbooks. Families can also use it for banking, shopping and contacting relatives. However, unreliable information, scams and harmful interactions can make careless use risky. A search result is not automatically trustworthy merely because it appears first. We should compare sources, check dates and avoid sharing private information unnecessarily. Strong passwords and sensible security habits protect accounts. Time management matters too, since entertainment can easily displace sleep and study. If an online experience becomes threatening, seeking help from a trusted adult is important. Access should also be affordable and inclusive so that learning opportunities do not depend entirely on family income. The internet is a powerful tool, but its benefits depend on judgement. Responsible users combine curiosity with caution and remember that other people deserve respect online as well as offline.

answers: The expression junk food is often used for foods that provide much energy but relatively little nutritional value. Frequently depending on foods high in salt, free sugars or unhealthy fats can make a balanced diet harder to maintain. However, judging a person's character from a snack is unkind and does not improve health. Food choices also depend on cost, time, availability and family circumstances. Schools can help by making safe drinking water and varied, affordable food available. At home, we can learn simple cooking skills and include a range of suitable foods rather than follow extreme diets. Reading labels, where available, can support informed choices. An occasional treat is different from an overall pattern of eating. Students should seek reliable guidance and avoid advertisements promising quick transformations. The goal is a practical, enjoyable and balanced diet, not fear of food or shame about body size. Small sustainable changes are often more useful than strict temporary rules.

Preparedness can save lives even when a hazard cannot be prevented. Communities need understandable early warnings, accessible shelters and clear evacuation plans. Families should know safe routes and keep essential information available. Students can take part in supervised drills and learn how to help without entering dangerous situations. Relief should reach people fairly, including those with disabilities and those living in remote areas. Long-term recovery requires more than distributing food for a few days; housing, health and education also need attention. We should avoid spreading unverified warnings or dramatic rumours. Knowledge, planning and cooperation can make communities more resilient and reduce the human cost of severe natural events.

Schools, hospitals and residential areas need particular consideration, but workers in noisy places require protection too. The solution is not simply to ask individuals to tolerate more disturbance. Drivers should avoid unnecessary honking, and event organisers should consider the comfort of neighbours. Students can keep personal audio at a safe level and take breaks from loud environments. A quieter community does not have to be lifeless. It can still celebrate, travel and work while respecting people's need for rest and communication. Thoughtful behaviour and consistent public management benefit everyone.

answers: A price hike is a noticeable rise in the cost of goods or services. When essential items become more expensive, families with limited incomes may struggle to meet daily needs. Prices can change because of production costs, shortages, transport problems, changes in demand or broader economic conditions. It is misleading to blame every increase on a single cause without evidence. Reliable market information and fair competition can help people understand and respond to the situation. Authorities should monitor dishonest practices while supporting an adequate supply of essential goods. Assistance may be necessary for households facing serious hardship. Families can plan purchases and reduce waste, but budgeting alone cannot solve a large loss of purchasing power. Students should learn basic financial judgement and avoid spreading rumours that encourage panic buying. Stable, affordable access to food and other necessities is important for health, education and social well-being, not merely for the convenience of individual shoppers.
